terms.current: The version or record in force right now.
terms.superseded: Replaced by a newer version; do not rely on it.
terms.protected: A protected surface or resource that should be reviewed.
terms.missing: A required check or artifact is absent.

group: Risk signals the model was given

terms.commit_point: The action is at the commit boundary (an external send, publish, durable or destructive write, cost action, privileged tool call, or final claim).
terms.conflicting_policy_versions: Both a superseded and a current policy version are present.
terms.low_reversibility_external: The action is hard to undo and reaches outside the workspace.
terms.medium_or_low_confidence: The agent's own confidence is below 0.75.
terms.protected_path_change: The action changes a protected path or resource.
terms.success_criterion_change: The action may change the thing that decides success, not the underlying work.
terms.changed_judge_without_product_fix: A test, eval, or scoring surface changed without a matching product fix.
terms.hidden_eval_data_access: The run touched held-out or leaked evaluation material.
terms.protected_surface_change: The action touches a protected surface that should be reviewed before commit.
terms.broad_unrelated_diff: The change is broader than the request and may hide unrelated edits.
terms.destructive_change: The action may delete or irreversibly alter stored state.
terms.sensitive_surface_access: The action accesses a sensitive surface with elevated privilege.
terms.suspect_evidence_used: A decision leaned on suspect evidence.
terms.secret_exposure_risk: Risk of exposing a secret, token, or credential.

terms.429: An HTTP error code meaning too many requests were sent.
terms.ECOA: US Equal Credit Opportunity Act (fair-lending law); "ECOA explainability" means the lender can state lawful reasons for a credit decision.
terms.disparate-impact audit: A fairness check that a decision does not systematically disadvantage a protected group.
terms.protected-class blinding: Attributes like race or gender are excluded from the decision's inputs.
terms.cohort band: The approved range for customers with a similar profile.
terms.build manifest: A record of which version each server or component runs.
terms.kill switch: A pre-wired way to stop a system instantly.
terms.code freeze: A period when production changes are prohibited.
terms.canary: A deliberately small first rollout to catch problems early.
terms.MIRI: JWST's Mid-Infrared Instrument, one of its onboard cameras and spectrographs.
terms.WASP-18b: A specific exoplanet; an astronomy target named in the claim.
terms.NHTSA: US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration; the vehicle-safety regulator.
terms.EEOC: US Equal Employment Opportunity Commission; the workplace-discrimination regulator.
terms.SOX: Sarbanes-Oxley Act; US law requiring strict financial-reporting controls.
terms.KYC: Know Your Customer; identity and legitimacy checks before onboarding a customer or partner.
terms.ATO: Australian Taxation Office; Australia's tax authority (in the income-averaging case).
terms.ACR: American College of Radiology; sets imaging-report standards.
terms.ECF: Electronic Case Filing; a court's electronic docket-submission system.
terms.MSA: Metropolitan Statistical Area; a US regional market unit (here, home-buying markets).
terms.LOS: Length of Stay; how long a patient stays admitted.
terms.AUC: Area Under the Curve; a 0-to-1 score of how well a model separates outcomes (higher is better).
terms.CAC: Customer Acquisition Cost; marketing spend to gain one customer.
terms.KPI: Key Performance Indicator; a tracked success metric.
terms.CTF: Capture The Flag; a hands-on security training exercise or competition.
terms.VLAN: Virtual LAN; an isolated network segment.
terms.BGP: Border Gateway Protocol; how internet routes between networks are announced.
terms.WAF: Web Application Firewall; filters and blocks malicious web traffic.
terms.CVE: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures; a public id for one known security flaw.
terms.CVSS: Common Vulnerability Scoring System; a 0-to-10 severity score (9.8 is critical).
terms.RCE: Remote Code Execution; a flaw that lets an attacker run code on a system.
terms.SQLi: SQL injection; an attack that injects malicious database commands.
terms.SQL injection: An attack that injects malicious database commands through an input.
terms.WebGoat: A deliberately vulnerable app used for security training.
terms.ODD: Operational Design Domain; the conditions a self-driving system is certified to handle.
terms.ADAS: Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems; assisted-driving features such as lane-keeping.
terms.VIN: Vehicle Identification Number; a car's unique serial number.
terms.WEA: Wireless Emergency Alerts; the system that pushes emergency alerts to phones.
terms.EHR: Electronic Health Record; a patient's digital medical chart.
terms.SNF: Skilled Nursing Facility; a post-hospital nursing-care facility.
terms.CNS: Central Nervous System; the brain and spinal cord.
terms.H1-receptor: A histamine receptor; blocking it gives antihistamine and sedative effects.
terms.PDB: Protein Data Bank; a public repository of 3D protein structures (a PDB ID names one).
terms.NAG: Standard sugar code (N-acetylglucosamine) in protein glycan annotations.
terms.AUP: Acceptable Use Policy; the rules for permitted use of a system.
terms.CAB: Change Advisory Board; the group that approves production changes (Emergency-CAB is the expedited form).
terms.SIGKILL: A Unix signal that force-kills a running process immediately.
terms.PID: Process ID; a number identifying one running process.
terms.OAuth: A standard for granting an app scoped access to your account without sharing your password.
terms.OpenAPI: A machine-readable spec describing a web API.
terms.JSDoc: A comment format that documents JavaScript or TypeScript code.
terms.SDK: Software Development Kit; libraries and tools for building on a platform.
terms.SRE: Site Reliability Engineer; the ops role that keeps production reliable.
terms.PoP: Point of Presence; a network edge location (PoP-LAX is the Los Angeles edge).
terms.OOB: Out-of-Band; a separate, independent channel or recovery path.
terms.LGTM: Developer shorthand for 'looks good to me' (an approval).
terms.egress: Outbound network traffic leaving a system.
terms.network egress: Outbound data leaving the system to the internet.
terms.allowlist: An approved list; only listed items are permitted.
terms.allow-list: An approved list; only listed entries are permitted.
terms.sandbox: An isolated environment that limits what code can access.
terms.CDN: Content Delivery Network; servers that deliver web content quickly.
terms.CI: Continuous integration; automated build-and-test on each code change.
terms.subnet: A subdivision of a network; a range of IP addresses.
terms.CIDR notation: Network shorthand for a block of IP addresses, like /24.
terms.penetration test: An authorized simulated attack to find security weaknesses.
terms.credential stuffing: An attack trying many stolen passwords to break into accounts.
terms.rate limit: A cap on how many requests are allowed per time window.
terms.DNS: Domain Name System; translates domain names into IP addresses.
terms.VPN: Virtual Private Network; a secure private network connection.
terms.serial console: A direct hardware port for managing a device.
terms.BGP community: A tag on internet routes that controls how they spread.
terms.peering: A direct traffic-exchange link between two networks.
terms.IAM: Identity and Access Management; controls who can do what.
terms.actor token: A credential identifying who is performing an action.
terms.service account: A non-human login identity used by automated software.
terms.secret rotation: Replacing a security credential on a schedule.
terms.vault: A secured system that stores passwords and keys encrypted.
terms.cron: A scheduler that runs computer tasks automatically at set times.
terms.sha256: A fingerprint code used to verify a file is unchanged.
terms.Nuclei: A tool that scans systems for known security vulnerabilities.
terms.malware classifier: An automated tool judging whether code is malicious.
terms.catastrophic backtracking: A regex flaw that makes a text search hang or crash.
terms.regex: A text-pattern language for searching and matching strings.
terms.dry run: A test execution that simulates changes without applying them.
terms.shadow traffic: Copying live traffic to test changes without affecting users.
terms.staged rollout: Releasing a change gradually to expanding user groups.
terms.halt-on-error: A safeguard that stops a rollout when a failure is detected.
terms.rolling deploy: Updating servers a few at a time to avoid downtime.
terms.API gateway: A server that manages and routes incoming API requests.
terms.kernel-load validation: Checking code loads safely into the OS core without crashing.
terms.biometric: Data measuring physical traits like faces or fingerprints for ID.
terms.face embedding: Converting a face image into a numeric identity code.
terms.two-person rule: A safeguard requiring two people to approve a critical action.
terms.dual-control: A rule requiring two separate people to approve a sensitive action.
terms.circuit breaker: A preset limit that automatically halts activity when a threshold is hit.
terms.change-management window: An approved time slot during which system changes may be made.
terms.provenance: The documented origin and history of a file or package.
terms.git blame: A version-control feature showing who last changed each line.
terms.diff: A view of what changed between two versions of code.
terms.codemod: A script that automatically rewrites code across many files.
terms.docstring: A documentation comment embedded in source code.
terms.structured logging: Recording events as machine-readable fields, not plain text.
terms.numpy: A Python library for fast numerical array computation.
terms.BioPython: A Python toolkit for working with biological data.
terms.RTL: React Testing Library; a tool for testing UI components.
terms.PGLite: A lightweight in-memory Postgres database used for testing.
terms.curl: A command-line tool for fetching data over the internet.
terms.argparse: A Python tool for reading command-line arguments.
terms.vectorized: Rewriting a loop into array math that runs much faster.
terms.ETL: Extract, transform, load; moving data between systems.
terms.JSONL: A file format with one JSON record per line.
terms.TSV: A tab-separated values text file, like a CSV.
terms.context window: The amount of text an AI model can read at once.
terms.system prompt: Hidden instructions that set how an AI assistant behaves.
terms.classifier: An automated tool that sorts inputs into categories.
terms.lazy-completion pattern: An AI habit of leaving work unfinished with placeholders.
terms.lazy-refusal pattern: An AI habit of declining a valid task to avoid effort.
terms.lazy-translate pattern: An AI habit of summarizing instead of fully translating.
terms.held-out split: Data set aside and never trained on, used only for testing.
terms.eval leakage: When test answers leak into training, inflating scores.
terms.contamination audit: A check for test data wrongly mixed into training data.
terms.clean split: Test data with no overlap with training data.
terms.dirty split: Test data contaminated by overlap with training data.
terms.good law: A court ruling still valid and not overturned, safe to cite.
terms.docket: A court's official record of filings in a case.
terms.affirmation page: A signed statement swearing a filing's contents are true.
terms.statute of limitations: The legal deadline for bringing a claim or case.
terms.motion in limine: A pretrial request asking a judge to exclude certain evidence.
terms.FRCP Rule 11: US court rule requiring attorneys to verify their filings are well-founded.
terms.sanctions order: A court ruling penalizing a party for misconduct.
terms.deferred prosecution agreement: A deal where charges are dropped if conditions are met.
terms.material omission: Leaving out information important enough to change conclusions.
terms.due process: The legal requirement to give fair notice and a chance to respond.
terms.statutory basis: The specific law that gives an agency authority to act.
terms.deposition: Sworn out-of-court testimony, often from a witness or expert.
terms.opposing counsel: The lawyer for the other side in a legal case.
terms.DOJ: US Department of Justice, the federal law-enforcement agency.
terms.false accounting: The criminal offence of falsifying financial records.
terms.trade secret: Confidential business information that gives competitive value.
terms.contestability path: A documented way to formally challenge or appeal a decision.
terms.First Amendment: US constitutional protection of free speech and the press.
terms.NYC Admin Code: The New York City Administrative Code, the city's body of laws.
terms.GDPR: EU law governing personal-data protection and privacy.
terms.DPIA: Data Protection Impact Assessment; a required privacy-risk review.
terms.DPO: Data Protection Officer; the role overseeing privacy compliance.
terms.ICO: The UK Information Commissioner's Office; the data-protection regulator.
terms.SA: Supervisory Authority; an EU national data-protection regulator.
terms.lawful basis: A legally valid reason required to process personal data under GDPR.
terms.SEC: US Securities and Exchange Commission; the stock-market regulator.
terms.CFTC: US regulator overseeing futures and derivatives markets.
terms.10-K: A company's annual financial report filed with the SEC.
terms.Form 8-K: An SEC filing disclosing major company events to investors.
terms.EDGAR: The SEC's public database of company filings.
terms.registered agent: Who legally accepts a company's official documents.
terms.LLC: Limited Liability Company; a US business structure.
terms.M&A: Mergers and acquisitions; buying or combining companies.
terms.writedown: An accounting charge reducing the recorded value of an asset.
terms.notional: The total face value of a trade, not the cash put up.
terms.order book: The live list of buy and sell offers for an asset.
terms.market depth: How much can be traded without moving the price much.
terms.hedge program: A set of trades made to offset financial risk.
terms.participation cap: A limit on how much of market volume one order can take.
terms.time-only slicing: Splitting a large order evenly over time regardless of volume.
terms.underwriting: The factors a lender weighs to decide credit terms and risk.
terms.credit utilization: The percentage of available credit a borrower is using.
terms.earnings call: A scheduled call where a public company reports results to investors.
terms.ATS: Applicant Tracking System; software that manages job candidates.
terms.SWE-II: Software Engineer level 2; a mid-level engineering job grade.
terms.four-fifths rule: Hiring-fairness test: a group selection rate must be at least 80 percent of another's.
terms.pass-through rate: Share of candidates who advance from one hiring stage to the next.
terms.adverse-impact analysis: Test for whether a practice unfairly disadvantages a protected group.
terms.protected attribute: A trait like race or age that law forbids using in decisions.
terms.protected-class proxy: A data field that stands in for a legally protected trait.
terms.screening model: An automated system that scores or filters job applicants.
terms.requisition: An open job posting that recruiters fill and then close.
terms.explainability: The ability to state the reasons behind an automated decision.
terms.target variable: The outcome a machine-learning model is trained to predict.
terms.triage: Assessing and prioritizing patients by urgency.
terms.post-discharge: After a patient leaves the hospital.
terms.attending physician: The senior doctor with primary responsibility for a patient.
terms.patient portal: A secure website where patients view records and messages.
terms.mammography: An X-ray exam of the breast to detect abnormalities.
terms.gestation: How far along a pregnancy is, counted in weeks.
terms.OB: Obstetrician; a doctor specializing in pregnancy and childbirth.
terms.fetal dose: The amount of radiation a fetus receives during imaging.
terms.lead shielding: A lead cover that blocks X-rays from part of the body.
terms.palpable: Able to be felt by hand on examination.
terms.Appropriateness Criteria: ACR guidelines on when an imaging test is warranted.
terms.diphenhydramine: The antihistamine drug sold as Benadryl.
terms.OTC: Over-the-counter; medicine sold without a prescription.
terms.therapeutic dose: The drug amount that is both safe and effective.
terms.Medicare Advantage: Private insurance plans that provide Medicare benefits.
terms.post-acute: Care after a hospital stay, such as rehab or nursing care.
terms.ALJ: Administrative Law Judge; hears appeals of agency decisions.
terms.Gy: Gray; the unit measuring absorbed radiation dose.
terms.MeV: Megaelectronvolt; an energy unit for radiation beams.
terms.linac: Linear accelerator; the machine that delivers radiation therapy.
terms.dosimeter: A device that measures radiation exposure.
terms.interlock: A safety mechanism that blocks operation unless conditions are met.
terms.mode confusion: When a machine operates in a different mode than intended.
terms.crystal structure: A 3D map of a molecule's atoms determined experimentally.
terms.antibody-antigen complex: An immune protein bound to the molecule it targets.
terms.residues: Individual amino-acid units that make up a protein chain.
terms.angstrom: A length unit of one ten-billionth of a meter, used for atoms.
terms.glycan: A sugar chain attached to a protein.
terms.MAN: Mannose; a sugar abbreviated in protein structure data.
terms.wafer-bin-map: A chip-factory map of which dies on a wafer passed testing.
terms.FSD: Full Self-Driving; Tesla's branded driver-assistance feature.
terms.turn-signal stalk: The lever behind the wheel that activates turn signals.
terms.ODD attestation: A signed confirmation that conditions are within the certified range.
terms.geofence: A virtual boundary defining where a feature may operate.
terms.occluded: Hidden from sensors by another object.
terms.telemetry: Automatically transmitted sensor or location data.
terms.secondary movement: A vehicle's follow-up motion after an initial collision.
terms.Zestimate: Zillow's automated estimate of a home's market value.
terms.iBuyer: A company that buys homes instantly using algorithmic pricing.
terms.Opendoor: A company that buys and resells homes algorithmically.
terms.regime detection: Analysis detecting when market conditions fundamentally shift.
terms.confidence interval: A statistical range showing how certain an estimate is.
terms.POS: Point of sale; the in-store system handling card and cash payments.
terms.inventory shrink: Loss of stock from theft, damage, or error.
terms.fleet management: Software for tracking and managing a company's vehicles.
terms.conversion pixel: Hidden tracking code reporting a user action to an ad platform.
terms.telehealth: Medical care delivered remotely, online or by phone.
terms.screener: A questionnaire that checks for signs of a condition.
terms.subscriber segment: A defined group of email recipients targeted together.
terms.supersession: Replacement of a record or claim by a newer authoritative version.
